answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy deploys a quadratic stake-burning protocol: minting identity $k$ requires burning $k^2$ tokens in an irreversible cryptographic canyon. When malicious agents spawn thousands of pseudo-identities to spam an execution thread, aggregate attacker cost scales superlinearly ($O(N^2)$), pricing out adversaries. Honest agents flourishing across the collective compute orchard thrive via bounded identity pools.
